body:
\`class-info\` now carries all 30 class keywords of [KEY=ROBJ_class](https://docs.intersystems.com/iris20262/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=ROBJ_class), and the grammar reads a class's keyword list as typed entries.

The keywords of one kind of declaration are one \`declaration_keywords!\` list in \`cos.rs\`: a bare name is a flag (\`Abstract\`, \`Not Abstract\`, \`Abstract = 0\`), \`Name = Shape\` takes a value parsed as the \`Shape\` grammar (\`ClassType\`, \`ClassList\`, \`Digits\`, ...). The names, the reading of an entry and the BNF a misfit value is reported against all follow from that list. An entry the list doesn't take stays in the tree with the reason (\`Typed<K> { entry, keyword: Result<K, KeywordIssue> }\`), so IRIS's own exports still parse whole and the checker reports what IRIS does with it:

\`\`\`objectscript
Class Demo.Keywords Extends %RegisteredObject [ Bogus, ClassType = Persistent, Inheritance = middle, CompileAfter = , System = x ]
\`\`\`

IRIS refuses a class only over \`ClassType\` (ERROR #7852, lowercase spellings only) and compiles past anything else in the list, dropping it:

\`\`\`
warning: 'Bogus' is not a class keyword, so IRIS ignores it; available: Abstract, ClassType, ClientDataType, ... [A6203]
error: 'Persistent' is not a value of 'ClassType'; expected "datatype" | "dynamic" | "index" | "literal" | "persistent" | "serial" | "stream" | "view" [A7718]
warning: 'middle' is not a value of 'Inheritance', so IRIS ignores it; expected "left"
title: Carry every class keyword, each read by a grammar of its own shape

body:
**Every unread assignment is reported.** Only the first was, so with

```
Set a = 1
Set b = 2
Set c = 3
```

a user fixed `a` and only then learned about `b`. Now each line gets `warning: Variable 'b' is assigned but never read [A5718]`.

**Arguments are read in source order.** `$PIECE` typed from/to before string/delimiter, `$LISTGET` the default before the position, `$ZF(-1)` the extra arguments before the program, so with two bad arguments the later one was reported and the earlier one hidden. `$PIECE(text, delimiter)` with both undefined now reports `text`.

**Two nits.** A routine's header range in the document outline came from the first line's byte length; it now comes from the OLC like every other position. The display of a term type had a stray `)`, and a label's procedure computed its return type twice.
title: Report every unread assignment, read arguments in source order, and tidy two nits

body:
Behavior-preserving compaction of the hand-written sources, leaving the grammar crate alone. 81 insertions, 174 deletions. Diagnostics over the whole type-check corpus are byte-identical to main's.

- Merged match arms with identical bodies: the operator result types and the operators a constant fold handles in `check_infix`, maybe-type merging, `ClsOrIns::name`, `maybe_defined`, `to_maybe_ty`, keyword naming, the DAO element walk, prefix operators, keyword style forms, and `store_check`.
- Replaced the three-way match in `check_set_member` with early returns, and dropped `check_prefix`'s unused flow parameter.
- Factored the branch-killing logic for a statically decided condition into one `settle`, used by both the constant and the union case.
- Derived `VariadicArg` from `Formal` through `NormalArg`'s conversion instead of repeating it.
- Put the wasm32 exclusion on `lib.rs`'s test module once instead of on fifteen items, and gave the three tests that opened the same two classes a shared setup.
title: Merge match arms that said the same thing, and share the test setup they repeated

body:
`$ZCONVERT(s, mode, table, handle)` keeps conversion state in its fourth argument. Measured on IRIS 2026.2:

```
Set out = $ZCONVERT(s, "O", "UTF8", h)      ; h undefined before, defined after: fine
Set out = $ZCONVERT(s, "O", "UTF8", st(1))  ; compile error #1010 Missing right parenthesis
Set out = $ZCONVERT(s, "O", "UTF8", ^st)    ; compile error #1011 Invalid name
Set out = $ZCONVERT(s, "O", "UTF8", 5)      ; compile error #1011 Invalid name
```

ascot already treated the handle as written, which is right, but said nothing about the other three. Each now gets

```
error: $ZCONVERT takes only a plain local variable as its handle [A4652]
```

Two guesses settled while there:

1. `ROUTINE X [Type=INT]` was recognized as compiler output by `INT` appearing anywhere in the header's type spec; it is now the grammar's `Type` value.
2. The member query had a retry without descriptions, for IRIS failing it over a description that starts with `{`, such as `/// {$$$CPFSave+...}` on `Config.Archives`'s `CPFFlags`. That failure (`ERROR #5035: General exception Name 'Parsing error'`) happens on Atelier v1 to v3 only; v4 and later return the row, and every ascot request goes through v8, so the retry and the closures that swapped the column in are gone.
title: Hold $ZCONVERT's handle to a plain local, and tighten two guesses

body:
ObjectScript converts a string to a number by its leading numeric prefix: `"3abc"` is 3, `"1.5"` is 1.5, `"abc"`, `" 1"` and `"-0"` are 0, and `=` compares strings (`"+2" = 2` is false, `"+2" + 0 = 2` true). All measured on IRIS 2026.2.

The constant folder parsed the whole string as an integer and fell back to 0, so `If "3abc"`, `If "1.5"` and `If "3abc" + 1 = 4` were all reported as always false (A8456) with the body unreachable. Now a string is the number it starts with; a negative, decimal or exponent prefix has no place in the folder's `u32`, so such a fold is left undecided rather than wrong, and truthiness reads the mantissa (`"0E5"` is false).
title: Read a string constant as the number it starts with

body:
Measured on IRIS 2026.2, at runtime and by compiling self-calls:

| index | Exists | Open / Delete |
|---|---|---|
| plain, bitslice, collatedkey, with or without a collation | yes | no |
| `[ Unique ]`, `[ PrimaryKey ]`, `[ IdKey ]` | yes | yes |
| the `IDKEY` every persistent class has unless it declares an id key; its argument is the id | yes | yes |
| bitmap, extent, or subscripted on a collection (`On Tags(ELEMENTS)`) | no | no |

A self-call to any other (`..NameIdxOpen("x")` on a plain index) is compile error MPP5392; through `$CLASSMETHOD` it is `<METHOD DOES NOT EXIST>`. ascot offered Open, Exists and Delete for every declared index and nothing for the implicit `IDKEY`, so such calls passed or failed the wrong way round; the two paths also disagreed on a collection key, and an IRIS key's collation (`Name:Exact`) stayed in its name.

`index-info` now mirrors the declaration (`Index name On keys [ keywords ]`): the `On` clause when there is one, each key with its optional `(KEYS)`/`(ELEMENTS)` subscript and `As` collation, then every index keyword from the reference (Abstract, Condition, CoshardWith, Data, Deferred, Extent, IdKey, Internal, PrimaryKey, ShardKey, SqlName, Type, Unique) as a flag or value. The workspace reads them from the keyword list, the Atelier side from `%Dictionary.CompiledIndex`, and one function derives the accessors for both. Breaking for a host that builds `IndexInfo`; declaration files move to version 4.
title: Describe an index as declared, and generate only the accessors IRIS does

body: Three reports picked a candidate by HashMap/HashSet iteration order, so the same file could get a different message on each run: which unread assignment (A5718) is reported when several are, which inconsistently declared variable (A8892) when two branches disagree on two, and which other file a duplicate class (A3717) points at when there are three. Now the first unread assignment in source order, the first inconsistent name alphabetically, and the smallest duplicate uri, as `unindex` already chose.
title: Report the same candidate every run

body:
IRIS evaluates any expression in an `#if` at compile time: `1-1`, `'$$$FLAG`, `$$$MODE="OUTPUT"`, `$SYSTEM.Version.GetMajor()>=2020`, all with ObjectScript truthiness. ascot decides only a literal `1` or `0` once the macros are expanded. Anything else used to leave both branches in the expanded text, checked as one straight line, so a `Quit` in the else branch made what followed "unreachable".

Rather than evaluate expressions at compile time, the directive now gets a hint (A5540) naming the condition as written and, when different, what it expanded to, and the first branch is taken. Every `#if` in the implicit `%systemInclude` closure expands to a literal, so no class gets the hint for just existing.
title: Say when an #if can't be decided, and go on with its first branch

body:
A pass over the checker for logic written more than once, with no change in what it reports: every diagnostic constructor is one expression; positions come from one `Positions` trait whether the text is a document, a method body or a bare OLC; the fixed-result builtin functions, the binding merges, the label details, the keyword lookups, the OLC conversions and the Atelier caching each go through one function; identical match arms and the nested Option/Result plumbing are folded. Net 1850 lines removed, 1070 added.

The one behavior change is in `check_block_body`: a label body is now paired with its own details, where a macro-headed label used to misalign every later pair.

Verified by the unit and live-IRIS tests and by the full diagnostic report over the internal corpus, which is identical to 0.4.3's.
title: Say each thing once in the checker

body:
A workspace's server connection and keyword style could only be set when constructing it, so a host had no way to tell ascot the server changed short of dropping the workspace and reopening every document.

- Added `set-env` to the workspace resource: replaces the server, drops every check, every routine expansion (they inline server includes) and the include caches, and returns every uri as stale.
- Added `set-style`: replaces the keyword style, drops every check, and returns every uri.

body: A9360 named the class the ancestry walk stopped at (e.g. `%Library.RegisteredObject`) instead of the receiver's class, and its "a superclass of" prefix tracked `##super` rather than whether that class was the receiver.
title: Name the receiver, not the unseen ancestor, in the unconfirmed-member hint

body:
Analyzing a workspace got several times slower after #117: every class implicitly includes `%systemInclude`, and `check_cls` fetched, parsed and expanded that include tree afresh for each class. On 28 classes sampled from the type-check corpus, main takes 2.92s and this branch 0.64s, with identical diagnostics.

- Cached the expanded implicit class includes once per workspace, dropped whenever an `.inc` document opens, changes or is removed, like `error_names`.
- Cached includes fetched from IRIS, parsed once and shared behind an `Arc`, so inherited and explicit includes such as `%occErrors` stop re-parsing per class.
- Cached class metadata fetched from IRIS per run behind an `Arc` (`Class::Iris(Arc<ClassInfo>)`), instead of re-fetching and cloning it on every lookup.
title: Resolve the implicit class includes once, and parse each IRIS include once

body:
Against IRIS 2026.1, the corpus disagreed with ascot on 18 annotations: arities the documentation and IRIS differ on, two severities IRIS doesn't share, a multidimensional property read or set with empty parentheses, and labels a `Goto` reaches inside a method.

- Fixed the arities to what IRIS runs: `$ZPOSITION` takes up to 3 arguments, `$ZWIDTH` up to 2, `$ZZENKAKU` from 1, `$WLENGTH` a delimiter as its second like `$LENGTH`, and `$ZDCHAR`, `$ZLCHAR`, `$ZQCHAR` and `$ZWCHAR` any number, encoding each like `$CHAR`.
- Added `UndocumentedArgument` (A5156, warning) for `$ZF(-1, command, more...)`: IRIS accepts the extra arguments and the documentation gives them no meaning. It lives in `$ZF(-1)`'s own grammar; no other function changes.
- Lowered `DuplicateClassName` (A3717) and `UnrecognizedParameterType` (A8317) to warnings: IRIS compiles both.
- Added `NodeWithoutSubscripts` (A3942): `..M()` on a `MultiDimensional` property throws `<OBJECT DISPATCH>` "missing subscripts" when read and fails to compile as a `Set` target.
- Held a label reached by `Goto` inside a method or procedure body to the body's returns, so its bare `Quit` is reported when the body promises a value; a `Do`ne label still returns for its caller. `LabelEntry` records which labels are nested, and `Flow::share_output` is what `tail_call` already did for fall-through.
title: Follow the corpus: arities, severities, empty subscripts, Goto targets
Release 0.4.2

body:
Both pinned in the corpus first (`ByFeature/Routines/Extrinsic`, `ByFeature/Routines/ProcedureBlock`).

- A label nested in a method or procedure block used to be held to the block's return shape. Whether it returns for the block (`Goto`) or for itself (`Do`) depends on how it is reached, which ascot doesn't track, so each now gets returns of its own like a routine-level label. That drops the false A6781 on a `Do`ne label's bare `Quit`, and also the true one on a `Goto` target's; the two corpus fixtures for the latter stay FAIL as known gaps.
- `$$Label` where the label has no formal parameter list raises `<PARAMETER>` on IRIS, with or without parentheses at the call, across routines and inside blocks; new A7604 reports it. An empty `()` on the label makes it a function. Labels read from IRIS don't carry the distinction, so they pass.
title: Assume nothing about a nested label's returns, and refuse $$ on a label without a formal list

body:
Three places where IRIS 2026.2 disagreed with ascot, each verified by compiling probes:

- NEW of a parameter in a procedure block is rejected (#1038) like any private variable, so A6866 now covers parameters too; only a PublicList variable may be NEW'd.
- A method body's `#define` stays in effect for the methods compiled after it, in name order, until `#undef`. ascot now follows that and warns at each such use (new A3904) instead of reporting an undefined macro; methods are checked in name order to match.
- `%occErrors` is not among the includes every class gets, so it is no longer implicit; `$$$ERROR` and the other compile-time macros still accept error names in their arguments, as IRIS resolves those itself.
title: Follow IRIS on NEW of parameters, method-body defines and the implicit includes
Drop three tests that only exercised a mocked IRIS

body: A private corpus now pins what ascot's diagnostic tests asserted. With that in place, 181 tests here that asserted only on diagnostics are removed, and CONTRIBUTING says the maintainer runs the corpus on diagnostic-changing PRs and before releases.
title: Move the diagnostic tests to the corpus

body:
Every member lookup went through one `get_obj_mem`, which took an `is_parameter` flag and an access kind and returned a union of value, collection and procedure that each caller then coerced, raising `ProcedureNotCalled` when the shape was wrong. IRIS tells the three member namespaces apart by syntax, so no caller could ever receive the wrong shape, and the coercion's error could not fire.

- Resolved members per namespace: `Parameters` yields a `Ty`, `Properties<Read | Assign | AssignNode | Called | Indexed>` a `PropertyTy` (a value, a `list Of`/`array Of` collection, or a multidimensional property), `Methods` a procedure. Each namespace converts its own declarations from the workspace or IRIS, names its `%Dispatch*` hook and types what the hook yields, and says which class names to qualify. `resolve_mem::<N>` is the one entry point; `HOTy`, `MemberTy`, `Visible`, `AccessKind`, `member_exists`, `member_suggestions`, `parameter_names` and `member_names` are gone.
- Resolved `..X(...)` as IRIS does: a method anywhere in the chain, then a property anywhere, which must be `MultiDimensional`, then `%DispatchMethod`. The old per-class interleaving let a subclass's multidimensional property shadow a superclass method; IRIS picks the method.
- Made the chain one iterator, `ancestry`: a class and its superclasses, nearest first and each once, resolved as they come. `find` is a `find_map` over it; `declared_in` reads one class's member from the workspace or IRIS alike; a miss suggests
title: Look members up by namespace, typed by what the namespace holds

body:
Fixes #112: ascot never sent IRIS's session cookie back, so every request opened a web session, each holding a license slot until it timed out.

- The agent keeps the cookie, so a connection uses one session.
- Dropping the connection ends the session. The CLI drops it before exiting, which `exit` would otherwise skip.
title: Keep one IRIS session per connection, and end it

body:
IRIS refuses to compile `New x` inside a procedure block (`#1038: Private variable not allowed`), but ascot only warned; and no code could reach `ProcedureCallReturnsNothing`, so the corpus could not cover it.

- Raised `NewInProcedureBlock` (A6866) from a warning to an error.
- Dropped `ProcedureCallReturnsNothing` (A7244): routine labels always return `Any`, so the one path that raised it never did. A void `$$label()` used as a value now reports `This value is undefined`, as a void method call already does.
title: Report NEW in a procedure block as an error

body: A release now commits the new formula to the tap's `master` instead of opening a pull request there.
title: Push the formula straight to the tap
Release 0.4.1

body:
Corpus tests IRIS's compiler rejects, which ascot let through. Each rule below was checked against IRIS 2026.1.

- A duplicate parameter name is an error, not a warning.
- `$NAME` and `$QUERY` of a procedure block's private variable are errors. A method's `PublicList` keyword was ignored, and is now read.
- `$ZF` takes no by-reference argument, `$ZSEARCH` takes one argument, and `SET $VECTOR` needs its type.
- An empty argument is an error where IRIS refuses one, by function and position, as measured for every intrinsic; `$$$LOWER()` expands to such a `$ZCONVERT` call.
- A property keyword that isn't `%Boolean` needs a value, as in `[ SqlComputeOnChange ]`.
- `Reset` isn't a generated property accessor.
title: Catch more of what IRIS refuses to compile

body:
A `#define`d macro called with more or fewer arguments than it takes was left unexpanded and unchecked, so `$$$ADDSC(sc)` or `$$$LOWER(s, s)` passed, where IRIS rejects both (MPP5614 and MPP5613).

- Too many and too few arguments are now errors at the call, A2716 and A6127. A `#def1arg` macro such as `$$$FormatText` takes its arguments as one, so it isn't counted.
- A method body's macro problems are now reported even when the expansion parses; until now only a routine's were.
title: Check a macro call's argument count against its definition

A tag released and published without running tests: `release.yml`, `publish-crates.yml` and `publish-npm.yml` only built.

IRIS's dictionary lists `%ClassName(fullname)` and similar without their defaults, so `..%ClassName()` warned `Too few arguments`; a `%Any` value failed `Cannot assign %Any to 'c' declared as %ClassDefinition`.

body: `[ Inheritance = right ]` is now honored for IRIS classes too, not only workspace ones. The bit is added to the WIT class record, which bridges ascot and its hosts.

body:
Fixes #98: an instance served with a certificate rustls's bundled roots don't cover, such as a company CA's or a self-signed one the machine trusts, was unreachable.

Certificates are now verified against the operating system's trust store, as browsers and curl do. A certificate the machine doesn't trust is still rejected; it can be installed there, or the instance reached over http.
title: Trust the OS's certificate store

body:
`get_cls` now returns a class's own members, indices and queries; ascot walks `extends` and the storage class (carried as `storage`) and synthesizes the generated members, as for workspace classes. Before, it read IRIS's flattened listing of every inherited and generated member per class.

This also speeds up `ascot declare` and compacts its files. Verified live on iris-community 2026.1 with a `%Persistent` subclass resolving inherited, storage and generated members.
title: Resolve IRIS classes like workspace classes

body:
Member resolution now follows IRIS's rules, each checked against iris-community 2026.1:
- `Extends (A, B)` takes A's member even when B overrides it; `[ Inheritance = right ]` takes B's. Before, the keyword was ignored.
- `..M` for a method `M` is an error; before, it resolved to the method.
- Property methods are the type class's class methods projected under the property name; before, every type got the same fixed list. `Query Q` gets `QFunc` and the `QExecute`/`QFetch` family; before, nothing.
- An `Index ... On` key that isn't a property is reported; before, it wasn't.
- A method beside a same-named multidimensional property is no longer a duplicate, since IRIS compiles it.
- Unread parameters and unassigned `Output`s of an overriding method are warned about again; before, an override suppressed both.
- `%RelationshipObject(ELEMENTTYPE=A)` and `(ELEMENTTYPE=B)` are different types that merge on their element types; before, they compared equal.
- The mask drops `%RegisteredObject.%OnNew` and `%SystemBase.%Dispatch*`, which the compiler doesn't recognize; before, the resolver special-cased the two classes by name.

Under the hood, one `lookup` replaces the seven hierarchy walks in `check/env.rs`: own declared members, then generated ones, then each direct superclass the same way in precedence order, stopping at an IRIS class (its entry is flattened) or one nobody can see. It takes the receiver and the namespace the syntax names, instantiates `This` and `..#PARAM` against th
title: Resolve members through one lookup, in IRIS's order

body:
`resolve_stubs` replaced a generated accessor's stub row, whose `Name` is the member's real name (`NameGet`), with the matching `%Dictionary.Compiled{Property,Query,Index,Constraint}Method` row, whose `Name` is only the short part (`Get`) and which has no `Origin` column. Every IRIS class therefore carried members called `Get`, `Set`, `IsValid` once per property, and `..NameGet()` never resolved against IRIS. In a 1 GB declaration dump of a USER namespace, these bare duplicates were 764K of 1.53M members.

The real row now keeps the stub row's name and takes the owning property's, query's or index's `Origin` through `parent->Origin`, which all four stub tables provide.

New live test: `Security.Users` has `%ConcurrencyGet` returning `%Library.RawString` with origin `%Library.Persistent`, and no bare `IsValid`. Verified against the CI image locally.
title: Keep generated accessors' names and origins from IRIS

body:
Without a file argument, `ascot declare` now prints where it is writing and uses `~/.ascot/<host>-<port>[-<prefix>]-<namespace>.d.json`, creating the directory. A bad URL or connection still fails before the path is resolved.

The declaration file also carries the instance's `$ZVERSION` as `iris_version`, read from the Atelier API listing. Files written before this load with it empty, so no regeneration is forced.

Verified end to end against a stub Atelier server; the live `tests/iris.rs` suite runs in CI.
title: Default `ascot declare` to ~/.ascot and record the IRIS version

body:
ascot has had one interface to its host, in the crate and in the WIT alike: three lookups of IRIS documents by their logical names.
- `get_cls`: a class's members and metadata
- `get_int_or_mac`: the source of a `.int` or `.mac` routine
- `get_inc`: the source of a `.inc` file

Hosts come in two kinds, and the one interface serves neither well:
- A host that already processes IRIS document content, like the language server, finds `get_int_or_mac` too low-level. What ascot needs is a routine's labels and their signatures, so the whole source crosses the boundary for nothing.
- A host that doesn't finds `get_cls` too high-level. It demands processing that ascot already knows how to do itself.

This PR replaces it with one interface per kind. `iris-context` has `get-cls`, `get-inc` and `get-rtn`, which returns a routine's labels. `atelier` has `query` and `get-doc`, the two Atelier REST API requests, from which ascot builds an `iris-context` itself. A workspace takes either.


A lookup or request can also fail, with a reason. The checker reports each failure as one hint, A4471, naming the class, routine or include file it could not look up and why, and takes it on trust. A lost connection used to turn every system class into an error.
title: Give the host a high-level and a low-level interface to IRIS

body:
Labels inside a routine procedure block (`Proc(x) public { ... Goto exitEarly ... exitEarly ... }`) used to stop the checker with "Type checking not implemented for 'Labels and subroutines'". They're now checked like a method body's labels.

- In a procedure (a routine's `{...}` block; a method unless `ProcedureBlock = 0`), every label returns for the body, so its `Quit` is held to the method's declared return type, or to whatever the procedure's first return established. That includes a label only ever `Do`ne: a bare `Quit` there is reported (a `Do` helper belongs at class level). A `Not ProcedureBlock` method's labels are subroutines like a routine's: their own returns, falling through into one another.
- Each label's scope entry carries its return expectation and the label that follows it, so fall-through hands the expectation on. Falling through into the next label is no longer reported in itself (only falling off the end with nothing to run into), and a label that falls through doesn't get "assigned but never read" for what the next one reads. One label's hard error no longer hides the next label's.
- `Goto` to a routine-level label from inside a procedure block is an error (IRIS: `<NOLINE>`). `Do`/`$$`, and `Goto label^routine`, may still leave the block; a nested label shadows a same-named outer one.
- Ranges over a `$$$Call(args)` that isn't a `#define`d macro (e.g. `$$$ERROR($$$MethodNotImplemented, ...)`) now map back to the source even when an argument's expansion
title: Check labels inside a routine's procedure blocks

On Windows the LSP's startup scan keyed files as `url::Url::from_file_path` spells them (`file:///C:/dir/Foo.cls`), while VS Code sends `file:///c%3A/dir/Foo.cls` for the same file. `Workspace::open` treated those as two documents declaring the same class: every opened `.cls` got a spurious "Class X is also declared in ..." error, and edits updated the editor's copy while other files kept resolving against the on-disk one.

Traced from the review, not reproduced on Windows (no Windows machine here). The unit test checks that `file:///c%3A/dir/Foo.cls` keys identically to the scan's spelling of the same path and no longer contains `%3A`, which is the mechanism, on any host.
